# Feature: Disclosure Review & Clarification Behavior

## 1. Feature Goal

**ID**: FEAT-105
**Source Plan**: `.spec-lite/plan_mvp.md`

Two promises, one feature, because they are the same promise seen from two sides: **the application never sends anything about a person's file that they have not read first, and it never guesses about something that changes what their answer means.**

Concretely:

- Before the first byte of file-derived context reaches a provider, the person sees **the literal text that will be sent** — not a summary of it, not an icon, the string itself — along with which provider and model will receive it. They approve it, or they do not run.
- That approval is pinned to an exact payload, an exact provider, and an exact model. Change the file, add a file, switch the model in Settings, and the approval is stale and the gate reopens. A repair attempt reuses it; a repair attempt does **not** widen it.
- When a failed run wants to send an error report so the agent can fix itself, that report has been through a **default-deny filter** that keeps exception types, frame locations, and library names and drops everything else. A traceback that reads `ValueError: could not convert string to float: 'N/A — see Jane's note'` leaves as `ValueError: could not convert string to float: <str len=21>`.
- When the file is ambiguous in a way that changes the answer — `03/04/2026` is either March or April, `amount` has 43 values that are not numbers, the workbook has four sheets — the application asks, in one screen, before it starts. When the ambiguity is cosmetic — which delimiter, whether a duplicate header got renamed — it decides, says what it decided, and offers an override.
- When the *agent* hits ambiguity mid-run it can ask too, through one custom tool, at most three times per execution, each question carrying its own proposed default. The fourth request is refused by the application and the agent proceeds with the default it already stated.

The load-bearing property, as in FEAT-104, is a negative one, but here it is enforced rather than merely true by absence: **there is exactly one function that assembles what goes into a prompt, and everything it emits is either the user's own words, an approved disclosure payload, filtered diagnostics, or application-authored text.** FEAT-106 and FEAT-108 call it. A test asserts nothing else can.

For the person running the preview, the visible change is: attaching `sales-q3.xlsx` to a task now opens a review screen that says *"Here is exactly what will be sent to Anthropic `claude-sonnet-5`: 14 KiB describing 12 columns and 10 rows of your 40,118. Two things I need you to decide before I start. Three things I decided for you."* — and the run does not begin until they press the button.

### Decisions applied (resolved 2026-09-21)

The plan lists FEAT-105 as blocked by **D04** (disclosure interaction, diagnostic filtering) and **D06** (question cap, handling of unresolved critical questions). Both were resolved with the user before this spec was written. Recorded here because `plan_mvp.md` §5 still lists them as open; each resolution is scoped to *this row* and does not close the decision globally.

| Decision | Resolution | Notes |
| --- | --- | --- |
| D04 — disclosure interaction | **Per task, re-asked on change.** One blocking review before the first send for a task. Repairs and diagnostics reuse that approval while the payload digest, provider, and model are all unchanged. A new or changed file, a different model, or a transmission kind the approval did not cover reopens the gate. | A five-attempt repair loop must not produce five modals — a person who is clicking through dialogs is not reading them, and a consent nobody reads is worse than none because it launders the decision. The approval is therefore *broad in time* (the task) and *narrow in content* (this exact payload, this exact model), which is the combination that keeps it meaningful. |
| D04 — diagnostic scope | **Granted at the same gate, as a separate, explicit, default-on choice**, shown with a real example of the filtered format. Declining it means a failed run stops and asks instead of auto-repairing. | "A failed run does not authorize sending the full dataset" (plan §3) is the requirement. Silently folding diagnostics into the context approval would technically satisfy "disclosed before sending" while defeating it in substance. Two scopes on one screen costs one checkbox and makes the repair path an explicit choice. |
| D04 — diagnostic filtering | **Structured allowlist, default-deny.** Only recognized structure survives: exception type, `File "<basename>", line N, in <fn>` frames, library names, ruff/bandit `path:line:col: CODE message` lines, and pytest failure lines. The exception message keeps its shape with every quoted literal replaced by `<str len=N>` and every digit run over four characters by `<num>`. Unrecognized lines are **dropped and counted**, never scrubbed-and-forwarded. | A scrubber is default-allow: it protects against the value shapes you anticipated, and row 40,000 contains a value the profiler never saw. An allowlist is default-deny: an unanticipated traceback shape leaks a dropped-line count, not a cell. The cost is repair signal, which is real and accepted — FEAT-106 gets exception type, location, and code, which is what a repair loop actually needs. |
| D06 — question cap | **Three agent-initiated questions per execution**, batched where the agent asks several at once, enforced **server-side at the tool boundary** by counting persisted questions — not by an instruction in a system prompt. The fourth is refused with a tool error telling the agent to proceed with the default it already supplied. | Enforcement by prompt is not enforcement. The count lives in the database, so it survives the model ignoring the rule, and the refusal is recorded in the transcript so a person can see the application declined to interrupt them. Separately, the pre-flight review screen may present **at most three required decisions** (see below); the two budgets are separate because they are different interactions — one screen before the run, versus interruptions during it. Say the word and they merge into one budget of three. |
| D06 — unresolved critical questions | **Wait indefinitely, but free the slot.** A `waiting` execution does not count toward `AUTOMATE_MAX_CONCURRENT_EXECUTIONS`; a separate provisional `AUTOMATE_MAX_WAITING_EXECUTIONS` caps parked runs. Answers persist per task, so a server restart — which kills the run, per FEAT-103's reconciliation — re-seeds them and the retry does not re-ask. Hitting the waiting cap declines the clarification rather than failing the run. | No timeout is invented: D14 owns time limits and has not been resolved. FEAT-103's concurrency default is `1`, so without the slot change one person at lunch blocks the whole application — the fix belongs here, in the row that introduces waiting. A provider-side session expiry during a long wait surfaces as FEAT-102's `failed` event; the existing TODO entry on agent session timeouts covers that and is not pre-empted here. |

### Assumptions carried (flag if wrong)

- **FEAT-105 replaces `PassthroughRunStrategy` as the default run strategy; FEAT-106 composes on top of the replacement.** FEAT-103 named `RunStrategy` as the seam and shipped a pass-through. This row ships `DisclosureRunStrategy`, which assembles the approved context, registers `request_clarification`, and still sends the user's own words as the task. It does **not** build a code-generation prompt, choose an output format, or run anything — FEAT-106 subclasses or wraps it. Building the gate without something on the other side of it would leave the gate untested.
- **The gate lives in task creation, not mid-run.** `POST /api/tasks` (FEAT-103) creates the task and starts the run in one call, so there is no window to approve after the task exists. The client fetches a preview for its staged uploads, the person approves, and the approval is submitted with the task. A text-only task with no uploads needs no gate at all — only the person's own words are sent — and requiring one there would train people to dismiss it.
- **Consent is verified twice, in two different places, by design.** The route rejects a missing or stale acknowledgement at `POST /api/tasks`; the prompt assembler independently refuses to emit file-derived context without a matching consent row. The second check is the one that holds when a future feature adds a code path the first one does not run through. This mirrors FEAT-104's four-place enforcement of its byte ceiling, for the same reason.
- **Pre-flight findings are recomputed server-side, never trusted from the client.** The browser sends `{findingId, choice}` pairs; the server re-derives the findings from the stored profile and matches by id. A client that invents a finding, or omits a required one, is rejected. The finding id is deterministic (`<profileId>:<column|sheet>:<kind>`) so it survives a page reload without server-side session state.
- **There is no stderr yet.** FEAT-108 owns execution and does not exist, so the diagnostic filter is built and proven against a **fixture corpus of real captured output** — CPython tracebacks including chained and `SyntaxError` forms, pytest failure blocks, ruff and bandit output — rather than against a live run. FEAT-106/108 feed it real bytes later; the contract and the tests are what this row owes them.
- **Clarification blocks the tool call.** `request_clarification.execute()` returns a promise resolved by the REST answer. The Pi session stays open for the duration, which is what keeps the agent's context intact and is why the slot accounting (not the session lifetime) is what changes. The promise is in-memory: a restart loses it, reconciliation marks the execution interrupted, and the persisted answers make the retry cheap. That is the honest behavior, and TASK-014 proves it rather than describing it.
- **`AgentSessionOptions.customTools` is assumed to exist and is specified here if it does not.** FEAT-102's TASK-001 lists the option fields without `customTools`, while its TASK-007 passes `customTools` to `createAgentSession` and FEAT-103's `RunStrategy.buildRun` returns one. The type is therefore implied by two rows and declared by neither. TASK-008 closes the gap explicitly, defining an SDK-free `AgentToolDefinition` in `packages/core` and mapping it inside the Pi adapter. If FEAT-102 lands with it already present, TASK-008's first step is a no-op — but it is not left to chance.
- **No retention or purge policy for consents and transmissions.** They cascade with the task and otherwise persist. D12 owns retention and is open; inventing a purge here would pre-empt it. Queued in TODO.md.

## 2. Data Model (Granular)

`.spec-lite/data_model.md` exists but, per `plan_mvp.md` §2, predates the confirmed decisions and is **not the authoritative schema** (reconciliation tracked in `.spec-lite/TODO.md`). It contains **no disclosure, consent, or clarification concept at all** — a grep for `clarif`, `disclos`, `consent`, and `question` returns nothing. Everything in this section is new, designed from the plan's confirmed policies and FEAT-104's profile output.

Conventions carried from FEAT-101/102/103/104: `snake_case` singular tables and columns; timestamps `INTEGER` epoch seconds with Drizzle `{ mode: 'timestamp' }`; booleans `INTEGER` with `{ mode: 'boolean' }`; JSON as `TEXT`; `INTEGER PRIMARY KEY AUTOINCREMENT`; schema defined in driver-independent `drizzle-orm/sqlite-core`.

### Entities & Attributes

- **disclosure_consent** — one recorded approval. The row that makes "they saw it first" a fact rather than a claim.
  - `id` (INTEGER) — `PRIMARY KEY AUTOINCREMENT`.
  - `task_id` (INTEGER) — `NULL` until the task is created (approval precedes it, exactly as an upload does). `FK → task.id ON DELETE CASCADE`.
  - `upload_ids` (TEXT) — `NOT NULL`. JSON array of the upload ids the approval covers, ascending. The set is part of the identity: approving two files does not approve a third.
  - `payload_digest` (TEXT) — `NOT NULL`. Lowercase hex SHA-256 over the **canonical serialization** of the rendered disclosure text. This is the whole enforcement mechanism: a byte that changes changes the digest, and a changed digest is a stale consent.
  - `payload_snapshot` (TEXT) — `NOT NULL`. The exact rendered text that was shown and approved, verbatim. Bounded by FEAT-104's 64 KiB ceiling per file. Kept so that "show me what I agreed to" is answerable months later, and so FEAT-110's history detail is not reconstructing it from a profile that may since have been re-parsed.
  - `byte_size` (INTEGER) — `NOT NULL`. Length of `payload_snapshot` in UTF-8 bytes; what the UI displayed.
  - `provider` (TEXT), `model` (TEXT) — `NOT NULL`. Who the approval named as the recipient. A person approving a send to a local model has not approved a send to a hosted one; a change to either invalidates the consent.
  - `scope_context` (INTEGER boolean) — `NOT NULL DEFAULT 1`. Permission to send the disclosure payload. Always granted (declining it means not running).
  - `scope_diagnostics` (INTEGER boolean) — `NOT NULL DEFAULT 0`. Permission to send filtered failure diagnostics on repair. The explicit second choice from the D04 resolution.
  - `granted_at` (INTEGER) — `NOT NULL DEFAULT (unixepoch())`.
  - `revoked_at` (INTEGER) — `NULL` unless withdrawn. Revocation is not a UI feature in this row; the column exists so that a revoked consent is expressible without a migration, and the verifier already treats a non-null value as no consent.
  - `created_at` (INTEGER) — `NOT NULL DEFAULT (unixepoch())`.

- **disclosure_transmission** — one receipt. Appended **before** the prompt is handed to the provider, never after, so a crash mid-send leaves a record that something was about to go rather than a silence.
  - `id` (INTEGER) — `PRIMARY KEY AUTOINCREMENT`.
  - `execution_id` (INTEGER) — `NOT NULL`, `FK → execution.id ON DELETE CASCADE`.
  - `consent_id` (INTEGER) — `NOT NULL`, `FK → disclosure_consent.id ON DELETE CASCADE`. Every transmission names the approval that authorized it. There is no such thing as an unauthorized transmission row.
  - `kind` (TEXT) — `NOT NULL`, `CHECK(kind IN ('context','diagnostics'))`.
  - `payload_digest` (TEXT) — `NOT NULL`. For `context`, equals the consent's digest, and the equality is asserted in code. For `diagnostics`, the digest of the filtered text.
  - `payload_snapshot` (TEXT) — `NULL` for `context` (the consent already holds the identical bytes; duplicating 64 KiB per attempt is waste), `NOT NULL` for `diagnostics`. `CHECK((kind = 'context' AND payload_snapshot IS NULL) OR (kind = 'diagnostics' AND payload_snapshot IS NOT NULL))`.
  - `byte_size` (INTEGER) — `NOT NULL`.
  - `summary` (TEXT) — `NOT NULL`. JSON: for `context`, `{files, tables, columns, sampleRows, truncations}`; for `diagnostics`, `{exceptionType, frameCount, droppedLineCount, maskedLiteralCount}`. What the receipt renders without expanding.
  - `provider` (TEXT), `model` (TEXT) — `NOT NULL`. Recorded again here rather than read through the consent, because this is the record of what actually happened, and the consent is the record of what was permitted. They must match; the code asserts it; storing both is what lets a test prove it.
  - `at` (INTEGER) — `NOT NULL DEFAULT (unixepoch())`.

- **clarification** — one question batch. Covers both sources, because the person answering does not care which part of the system was confused.
  - `id` (INTEGER) — `PRIMARY KEY AUTOINCREMENT`.
  - `execution_id` (INTEGER) — `NOT NULL`, `FK → execution.id ON DELETE CASCADE`.
  - `source` (TEXT) — `NOT NULL`, `CHECK(source IN ('preflight','agent'))`. `preflight` is the application asking from FEAT-104's profile notes; `agent` is the model asking through the tool.
  - `call_id` (TEXT) — the FEAT-102 tool `callId`, so the batch joins to the `tool_started`/`tool_finished` events in the transcript. `NULL` for `preflight`.
  - `status` (TEXT) — `NOT NULL DEFAULT 'pending'`, `CHECK(status IN ('pending','answered','declined','cancelled','interrupted'))`. `declined` is the application refusing to ask (cap reached or no waiting capacity) — recorded, not silent, because an invisible refusal is indistinguishable from a model that never asked.
  - `decline_reason` (TEXT) — `NULL` unless `declined`. `CHECK(decline_reason IS NULL OR decline_reason IN ('question_limit','waiting_capacity'))`.
  - `asked_at` (INTEGER) — `NOT NULL DEFAULT (unixepoch())`.
  - `settled_at` (INTEGER) — `NULL` until answered, declined, cancelled, or interrupted.
  - `created_at` (INTEGER) — `NOT NULL DEFAULT (unixepoch())`.

- **clarification_question** — one question and its answer. Normalized rather than a JSON blob on the batch for two concrete reasons: the three-per-execution cap is enforced by `COUNT(*)` over this table joined to `clarification`, and FEAT-111's re-run seeding looks up prior answers by `finding_key`.
  - `id` (INTEGER) — `PRIMARY KEY AUTOINCREMENT`.
  - `clarification_id` (INTEGER) — `NOT NULL`, `FK → clarification.id ON DELETE CASCADE`.
  - `position` (INTEGER) — `NOT NULL`. 0-based order within the batch.
  - `finding_key` (TEXT) — `NULL` for agent questions; for pre-flight, the deterministic `<profileId>:<target>:<kind>` id. Stable across reloads and across re-runs of the same file, which is what makes seeding possible.
  - `impact` (TEXT) — `NOT NULL`, `CHECK(impact IN ('data_loss','meaning'))`. Cosmetic findings never become questions — they become applied defaults. The CHECK is the D06 rule expressed as a constraint: a cosmetic question cannot be stored, so it cannot be asked.
  - `prompt_text` (TEXT) — `NOT NULL`. The question. For agent questions this is **model output and therefore untrusted input to the DOM**.
  - `rationale` (TEXT) — `NOT NULL`. Why it changes the meaning or risks data loss. Required from the agent by the tool schema; generated from the finding table for pre-flight.
  - `options` (TEXT) — `NULL` for free-text, otherwise JSON `[{value, label}]`, at most 6.
  - `proposed_default` (TEXT) — `NOT NULL`. What happens if this is declined or unanswered. Required — a question with no default is a question the application cannot decline, and declining is a behavior this feature depends on.
  - `answer` (TEXT) — `NULL` until answered. For an options question, one of the option values; for free text, the person's words, capped at 2,000 characters.
  - `answer_source` (TEXT) — `NULL` until settled, then `CHECK(answer_source IN ('user','default','seeded'))`. `seeded` means carried from a prior execution of the same task — visible, never silent.
  - `answered_at` (INTEGER) — `NULL` until settled.
  - `created_at` (INTEGER) — `NOT NULL DEFAULT (unixepoch())`.

### Modified entity

- **conversation_event** (FEAT-103) — `kind`'s `CHECK` gains `'clarification_requested'`, `'clarification_answered'`, and `'disclosure_sent'`. These are **application-owned** kinds, exactly like the existing `user_prompt` and `state_changed`; FEAT-102's `AgentEvent` union is untouched, and its type-level test asserting exactly five members continues to pass. SQLite cannot alter a `CHECK` in place, so migration `0003` performs the standard table rebuild — and TASK-005 asserts existing rows survive it, because a migration that silently empties a transcript would be discovered by a user, not by a test.

### Relationships

- `task` 1:N `disclosure_consent` via `disclosure_consent.task_id` (`ON DELETE CASCADE`, nullable before the task exists). Normally 1:1; a second row appears when a consent went stale mid-task and was re-granted.
- `disclosure_consent` 1:N `disclosure_transmission` via `disclosure_transmission.consent_id` (`ON DELETE CASCADE`).
- `execution` 1:N `disclosure_transmission` via `disclosure_transmission.execution_id` (`ON DELETE CASCADE`).
- `execution` 1:N `clarification` via `clarification.execution_id` (`ON DELETE CASCADE`).
- `clarification` 1:N `clarification_question` via `clarification_question.clarification_id` (`ON DELETE CASCADE`).
- `disclosure_consent` N:M `upload` — expressed as the `upload_ids` JSON array, not a join table. The set is immutable once granted, is never queried by upload, and a join table would imply an editability the design forbids.

### Indexes & Constraints

- `INDEX disclosure_consent_task ON disclosure_consent(task_id)` — the verifier's lookup ("is there a live consent for this task?") on every prompt assembly.
- `UNIQUE INDEX disclosure_consent_digest ON disclosure_consent(task_id, payload_digest, provider, model) WHERE revoked_at IS NULL` — partial and unique: re-approving the identical payload for the identical model on the identical task is idempotent rather than duplicating rows, and a revoked row does not block a fresh grant.
- `INDEX disclosure_transmission_execution ON disclosure_transmission(execution_id)` — the receipt list for one run; FEAT-110 leans on it.
- `INDEX clarification_execution ON clarification(execution_id)`.
- `UNIQUE INDEX clarification_call ON clarification(call_id) WHERE call_id IS NOT NULL` — one batch per tool call; a duplicate means the tool fired twice for one `callId`, which is a bug and must surface as one.
- `UNIQUE INDEX clarification_question_position ON clarification_question(clarification_id, position)`.
- `INDEX clarification_question_finding ON clarification_question(finding_key) WHERE finding_key IS NOT NULL` — FEAT-111's seeding lookup, and this row's own "did we already ask this?" check.
- `CHECK(byte_size >= 0)` on both `disclosure_consent` and `disclosure_transmission`.
- `PRAGMA foreign_keys = ON` comes from FEAT-101's client, so the cascade `task → disclosure_consent → disclosure_transmission` and `execution → clarification → clarification_question` are real. TASK-005 asserts both by row count.
- **Invariant enforced in code, asserted in tests**: no `disclosure_transmission` row may exist whose `consent_id` points at a row with `revoked_at IS NOT NULL`, whose `provider`/`model` differ from the consent's, or — for `kind = 'context'` — whose `payload_digest` differs from the consent's. This is the D04 policy expressed at the persistence boundary, so a violation fails a test rather than quietly sending something nobody approved.
- **Invariant enforced in code, asserted in tests**: at most `AUTOMATE_MAX_AGENT_CLARIFICATIONS` questions exist across all `source = 'agent'` clarifications for one execution. Counted, not assumed.

### Storage layout

FEAT-105 adds **no new directories and writes no files.** Consents, receipts, questions, and answers live in `data/automate.db`. The one thing this feature could plausibly have written to disk — a log of what was sent — is deliberately *not* written to disk, because a plaintext file of everything ever disclosed is a worse privacy exposure than the disclosure it audits, and the database row already answers the question.

## 3. Files

**`packages/core`** (platform-agnostic — `packages/web` imports it, so no Node built-ins and no Pi SDK)

- `src/disclosure/limits.ts` — the named constants fixed by D04/D06: agent question cap, pre-flight decision cap, diagnostic byte and frame caps, answer length cap, option count cap.
- `src/disclosure/canonical-json.ts` — deterministic serialization (sorted keys, no insignificant whitespace, stable number formatting) so the digest of equal content is equal on every platform.
- `src/disclosure/disclosure-text.ts` — `renderDisclosureText(payloads, options): string`. Turns FEAT-104's `DisclosurePayload[]` into the exact block that goes into a prompt. **The single rendering authority** — the review screen shows its output and the prompt contains its output, so they cannot drift.
- `src/disclosure/ambiguity.ts` — `classifyFindings(profiles): { required, defaults, notices }`, the pure mapping from FEAT-104 profile notes and column flags to `data_loss` / `meaning` / `cosmetic` findings, with deterministic `findingKey`, severity ordering, question text, options, and proposed defaults.
- `src/disclosure/diagnostic-filter.ts` — `filterDiagnostics(raw, options): FilteredDiagnostic`, the default-deny allowlist and the literal masker.
- `src/disclosure/prompt-context.ts` — `assemblePromptContext(input): PromptContext`, the single chokepoint for everything entering a prompt, plus the `PromptContextSource` union that names its only four permitted inputs.
- `src/disclosure/consent.ts` — `DisclosureConsentView`, `ConsentStaleness` (`'none' | 'digest' | 'model' | 'scope' | 'revoked'`), and `evaluateConsent(consent, required)`, pure so both server and client can explain staleness with identical words.

**Docs**

## 4. Dependencies

- **FEAT-101** — required in full: `AutoMateError`/`ERROR_CODES`, the Pino logger and its redaction, `createApp` + the error envelope + correlation-id middleware, the Drizzle/`node:sqlite` client and the migration pipeline, the repository pattern, TanStack Router/Query, the typed API client, and the `ds.*` design tokens.
- **FEAT-102** — required for the provider seam: `AgentSessionOptions`, the `customTools` channel and the `AgentToolDefinition` type (closed by TASK-008 if absent), the `tool_started`/`tool_finished` events the clarification surfaces through, `createSanitizer` for outbound payloads, the configured provider's current `provider`/`model` (which the consent pins), and `FakeAgentProvider`, which is how every test here runs a scripted tool call with no network.
- **FEAT-103** — required for `task`, `execution`, `conversation_event`, the state machine and its `waiting` member, `TaskSession` and `TaskSessionRegistry`, the `RunStrategy` seam this row fills, `POST /api/tasks`, the WebSocket transport that carries the new event kinds unchanged, the origin guard applied to the new state-changing routes, and the composer.
- **FEAT-104** — required for `upload`, `upload_profile`, `upload_column`, `DisclosurePayload` and `buildDisclosurePayload`, the structured `notes` and column flags the ambiguity classifier reads, and the staged-upload flow the gate sits in front of.
- **External**: **none.** No new runtime dependency. The digest uses `node:crypto` (already available in `packages/server`), canonical serialization is a dozen lines, and the filter is string work. A dependency here would be a dependency inside the privacy boundary, which is the last place to add one.

### Not dependencies (deliberately)

- **A schema-validation or PII-detection library.** The filter is an allowlist, so it has nothing to detect — it keeps what it recognizes and drops the rest. A PII detector is a default-allow tool and would invert the property this feature exists to hold.
- **A crypto library.** `node:crypto`'s SHA-256 is the whole requirement, and the digest is an integrity check against accidental drift, not a defense against a motivated local attacker who already has the database file.
- **FEAT-106/107/108** — this row is provable end to end with no code generation, no verification, and no Python: a file is attached, the gate is approved, the approved text reaches a fake provider, a scripted tool call parks the run, an answer resumes it, and receipts record every byte. The diagnostic filter is proven against captured fixtures because there is nothing running yet to produce live output.

### TASK-002: Ambiguity classifier over FEAT-104 profile notes

- [ ] **Implementation**: Add `src/disclosure/ambiguity.ts` exporting `classifyFindings(profiles: readonly TableProfile[]): { required: Finding[]; defaults: AppliedDefault[]; notices: Notice[] }`. Implement exactly this mapping, and no heuristics beyond it: `ambiguous_date_format` → **meaning**, options `DD/MM` / `MM/DD`, default the interpretation the profiler ranked higher; more than one non-empty sheet → **meaning**, options one per sheet, default the first visible non-empty sheet; a hidden sheet holding data → **meaning**, options include/exclude, default exclude; `no_header_detected` → **meaning**, options "row 1 is data" / "row 1 is a header", default data; a column with `is_mixed_type` and more than 1% offending values → **meaning**, options treat-as-text / drop-offending / stop, default treat-as-text; `ragged_row_count > 0` → **data_loss**, options keep / skip, default keep; `merged_cell_count > 0` → **meaning**, options continue / stop, default continue; `duplicate_headers_renamed`, sniffed delimiter and quote, detected encoding, `leading_blank_rows_skipped`, and `blank_row_count` → **cosmetic**, emitted as `AppliedDefault` with an override value, never as a question; `row_cap_reached` and `rowCountExact === false` → `Notice`, which states that statistics cover part of the file and carries no decision. Compute `findingKey` as `<profileId>:<target>:<kind>` with `target` being the column name or sheet index, and assert it is stable across two calls on the same input. Order `required` by impact (`data_loss` first), then profile index, then column position, and return **at most `MAX_PREFLIGHT_DECISIONS`**, moving the remainder into `defaults` with their proposed default applied and a flag marking them as demoted, so an eight-ambiguity file produces three questions and five disclosed decisions rather than an interrogation. Keep the module pure — no clock, no randomness, no I/O.
- [ ] **Unit Tests**: Each mapping row above, driven from a literal profile fixture, asserting impact, options, default, and question text. A clean profile yields no required findings and no defaults beyond the sniffed dialect. A profile with two ambiguous dates and one ragged-row finding orders the ragged finding first. A profile with eight meaning-level findings returns exactly three required and demotes five, and the demoted five carry their defaults. `findingKey` is identical across two calls and differs when the column name differs. A mixed-type column at exactly 1% and just over it fall on the documented sides of the boundary. A single-sheet workbook produces no sheet question; a two-sheet workbook where one sheet is empty produces none either. A cosmetic finding can never appear in `required`, asserted over a generated matrix of profiles — this is the D06 rule under test.
- [ ] **Documentation Update**: Invoke **Document** update mode for ambiguity classification.
- **Verify**: `pnpm --filter @automate/core test ambiguity` passes; a property test over generated profiles asserts `required.length <= MAX_PREFLIGHT_DECISIONS` and that every `required` entry has a non-empty `proposedDefault`.

### TASK-003: Diagnostic filter — default-deny allowlist over raw failure output

- [ ] **Implementation**: Add `src/disclosure/diagnostic-filter.ts` exporting `filterDiagnostics(raw: string, options): FilteredDiagnostic` where the result carries `exceptionType`, `message` (masked), `frames: [{file, line, function}]`, `libraries`, `checks: [{path, line, col, code, message}]`, `testFailures`, `droppedLineCount`, `maskedLiteralCount`, `truncated`, and `text` (the rendered form that goes into a prompt). Recognize, and keep, exactly: CPython traceback headers including `During handling of the above exception` and `The above exception was the direct cause`; `  File "<path>", line N, in <fn>` frames, **reduced to the basename** of the path; the terminal `ExceptionType: message` line; ruff/bandit `path:line:col: CODE message` lines; and pytest `FAILED <file>::<test> - <ExceptionType>: <message>` lines. **Drop every other line and count it.** Mask inside every surviving message: any single- or double-quoted span → `<str len=N>`; any digit run longer than four characters → `<num>`; leave short integers intact, because "expected 3 columns, got 7" is the signal and destroying it would make the filter useless rather than safe. Never emit a source line from the traceback's code context — that is generated code, but it is interleaved with data in f-strings and is not worth the analysis. Cap at `MAX_DIAGNOSTIC_FRAMES` frames (keeping the innermost and outermost and recording the elision) and `MAX_DIAGNOSTIC_BYTES` total, marking `truncated`. Keep the module pure. Write the header comment stating the invariant: **this function is an allowlist; a line it does not recognize is dropped, never forwarded, and adding a "pass through anything else" branch defeats the feature.**
- [ ] **Unit Tests**, driven from `src/disclosure/__fixtures__/diagnostics/` holding real captured output: a `ValueError: could not convert string to float: 'N/A — see Jane's note'` yields `ValueError` with the quoted span masked and its length recorded, and the person's name appears nowhere in the output — asserted by substring search over the whole serialized result, which is the central test of this task; a chained traceback keeps both exception types and both frame sets; a `SyntaxError` with its caret line keeps the type and location and drops the caret and the source line; a `KeyError: 'customer_email'` masks the key (a column name is still the user's data); absolute Windows and POSIX paths are reduced to basenames, asserted against the OS path root appearing nowhere; a pandas traceback keeps the library frames and drops the interleaved data preview block that pandas prints; ruff and bandit lines survive with their codes; a pytest block keeps the failure lines and drops the captured-stdout section; 200 frames truncate to the cap with the elision recorded; a 5 MB input is filtered without throwing and lands under the byte cap; an empty string, a string of only unrecognized lines, and binary noise each return a valid result with everything counted as dropped; filtering an already-filtered result is idempotent.
- [ ] **Documentation Update**: Invoke **Document** update mode for diagnostic filtering.

Then add `src/disclosure/clarification-service.ts` and `src/disclosure/clarification-tool.ts`. The tool's parameter schema requires `questions: [{ question, rationale, impact: 'data_loss' | 'meaning', options?: [{value,label}], proposedDefault }]`, 1–3 entries, each field non-empty — a question with no `proposedDefault` or no `rationale` is rejected by the schema, so the model cannot ask something the application is unable to decline. `execute` calls `ClarificationService.ask(executionId, callId, questions)`, which: rejects a batch that would take the execution past `AUTOMATE_MAX_AGENT_CLARIFICATIONS` **counted from the database**, persisting the batch as `declined` with reason `question_limit` and returning a tool result telling the agent to proceed with its stated defaults; rejects when parked runs are at `AUTOMATE_MAX_WAITING_EXECUTIONS`, persisting `declined` with reason `waiting_capacity` and the same instruction; otherwise persists the batch `pending`, appends a `clarification_requested` conversation event, transitions the execution `generating → waiting`, registers a pending promise keyed by clarification id, and awaits it. On answer it returns a structured result pairing each question with its answer. On abort it rejects the promise so the tool call unwinds and the run settles `aborted`. The promise registry is in-memory and is explicitly not durable — a restart is handled by FEAT-103's reconciliation plus `markInterrupted`.

Answering resolves the tool promise with a result pairing questions to answers; aborting rejects it and the execution settles `aborted`; a second `execute` for the same `callId` hits the unique index and surfaces as an error rather than opening a second batch. ### TASK-009: `waiting` state, slot accounting, and recovery

- [ ] **Implementation**: Extend `packages/core/src/conversation/execution-state.ts` with `generating → waiting`, `waiting → generating`, `waiting → aborted`, and `waiting → failed`; every other transition into or out of `waiting` stays invalid. Modify `TaskSession` to emit `state_changed` on each, to append `clarification_requested` and `clarification_answered` events at the next `seq` through the existing persist-before-broadcast path, and to keep the text coalescer flushed before a parking event so a partial sentence never lands after the question. Modify `TaskSessionRegistry`: `activeCount()` excludes sessions whose execution is `waiting`, so a parked run frees its concurrency slot; add `waitingCount()` and `AUTOMATE_MAX_WAITING_EXECUTIONS` (provisional default `5`, documented in the README as pending D14 and not a resolution of it); `abort(executionId)` on a parked session cancels the pending clarification first, then aborts the session; `drain(timeoutMs)` cancels pending clarifications before aborting, so shutdown does not wait on a person; `reconcileOnStartup()` additionally marks every `pending` clarification of an interrupted execution as `interrupted`, so a resumed page shows a settled question rather than a form that will never submit. Extend the interrupted message for a waiting execution to say the answers were kept: *"This run was interrupted while waiting for your answer. Your answers were saved — start it again and you will not be asked twice."*
- [ ] **Unit Tests**: The transition table accepts the four new edges and rejects `pending → waiting`, `waiting → completed`, and `completed → waiting`. A parked session does not count toward the concurrency cap, asserted by starting a second execution at cap 1 while the first is waiting; the second execution parking while the first is also parked is refused at the waiting cap. Answering a parked run returns it to `generating` and the transcript shows `state_changed`, `clarification_requested`, `clarification_answered`, `state_changed` in that order with gap-free `seq`. Aborting a parked run cancels the clarification, settles `aborted`, and frees both counts. `drain` cancels a pending clarification rather than waiting for it. `reconcileOnStartup` over a `waiting` execution marks it `failed`/`EXECUTION_INTERRUPTED`, marks its clarification `interrupted`, appends the terminal `state_changed`, leaves the answered questions intact, and is idempotent when run twice. Pending assistant text is flushed before the `clarification_requested` event, asserted by `seq` order.

## 6. Cross-Cutting Concerns

- **Data disclosure (D04) — this row *is* the concern.** FEAT-104 built a bounded payload and transmitted nothing; FEAT-105 is the first row where user-derived content actually leaves the machine, and it is gated in four independent places so no single mistake defeats it: the route rejects task creation without a matching acknowledgement (TASK-007); `verifyForTransmission` independently refuses to build a prompt without a live, digest-matched, model-matched consent (TASK-011); the persistence layer rejects a transmission row that contradicts its consent (TASK-005); and `assemblePromptContext` is the only construction site, enforced by a repo scan (TASK-014). The diagnostic path is default-deny rather than scrubbed (TASK-003), so an unanticipated output shape costs repair signal, not privacy. The property that ties it together: **what was shown and what was sent are the same bytes**, because the prompt is built from the approved snapshot rather than re-rendered.
- **Clarification behavior (D06) — the other half of the concern.** Cosmetic ambiguity is decided, disclosed, and overridable; meaning-changing and data-loss ambiguity is asked. The rule is enforced structurally, not by instruction: `clarification_question.impact` has no `cosmetic` value, so a cosmetic question cannot be persisted; the agent's tool schema requires a rationale and a proposed default, so a question the application cannot decline cannot be asked; and the three-per-execution cap is a `COUNT(*)`, so a model that ignores its system prompt still cannot interrupt a fourth time. Every refusal is recorded and rendered, because an invisible refusal is indistinguishable from a question nobody asked.
- **Auth**: N/A — single-user local deployment, no accounts (memory, D03). The protection added is FEAT-103's `Origin`/`Host` guard extended to the new state-changing routes, which matters here specifically: without it a page in the developer's own browser could grant a disclosure consent or answer a clarification on their behalf. Not a full answer to D10; the per-install loopback token remains open and tracked in TODO.md.
- **Error Handling**: New errors extend `AutoMateError` — `DISCLOSURE_CONSENT_REQUIRED`, `DISCLOSURE_CONSENT_STALE`, `DISCLOSURE_SCOPE_NOT_GRANTED`, `PREFLIGHT_DECISION_REQUIRED`, `CLARIFICATION_NOT_FOUND`, `CLARIFICATION_NOT_PENDING`, `CLARIFICATION_INVALID_ANSWER`, `CLARIFICATION_LIMIT_REACHED`, `WAITING_CAPACITY_REACHED`. FEAT-101's middleware is the only place that formats an error body. Every gate error names the concrete change and the next step — "the model changed from `claude-sonnet-5` to `gpt-5` since you approved this; review what will be sent and approve again" — because the audience cannot read a stack trace and a bare "consent invalid" is a dead end. A declined clarification is **not** an error: it is a recorded outcome with a default, and it never fails a run.
- **Logging**: Pino. `info` — consent granted (task id, byte size, provider, model, scopes; **never the payload**), transmission recorded (execution id, kind, byte size, digest), clarification opened/answered/declined (ids, counts, reason). `warn` — a stale or missing consent blocked a run, a clarification was declined for cap or capacity, an answer arrived for a settled batch. `error` — unexpected failures with the correlation id the client received. `debug` — finding kinds and counts, **never their text**. **Never logged**: the disclosure payload or snapshot, question text, answer text, filtered diagnostic text, sample values, or original filenames. This is the same rule FEAT-102/103/104 set and it binds harder here: the whole point of a 64 KiB bound is defeated if the same bytes land in an unbounded log file. The database row is the audit record; the log carries ids and sizes.
- **Security — untrusted rendered content**: Three distinct untrusted sources converge on this UI. Sample cells come from the user's own file (FEAT-104's rule: text only). Clarification questions and options are **model output** (FEAT-103's rule: text only, no raw HTML, no `dangerouslySetInnerHTML`). Filtered diagnostics originate in generated code's output. All three render as text; TASK-012 and TASK-013 test script, `onerror`, `javascript:`, and formula payloads directly in each path.
- **Security — the consent is not a security boundary against the local user.** Anyone who can run the application can grant a consent, and the digest defends against accidental drift (a re-parse, a model change, a stale tab), not against someone editing the database. Saying otherwise would be the same category error as calling a uv virtualenv isolation.
- **Cancellation (plan §6)**: A parked run is cancellable through the **existing** `POST /api/executions/:id/abort` — no second cancel path. Abort cancels the pending clarification first so the blocked tool call unwinds, then aborts the provider session. `drain` does the same on shutdown rather than waiting on a person. This extends FEAT-103's generation leg; the generated-test, dependency-preparation, and execution legs remain FEAT-106/108's and attach to the same endpoint.
- **State recovery (plan §6)**: Browser disconnect — the parked run survives; reconnect replays from `lastSeq` and the pending clarification is re-fetched over REST, so the form comes back. Server restart — no run resumes; `waiting` is already in FEAT-103's active partial index, so reconciliation marks the execution interrupted and this row additionally settles its pending clarification as `interrupted` and says so in plain English. **Answers persist**, so the retry seeds them and the person is not asked twice. That is the concrete compensation for having no durable wait.
- **Provenance (plan §6)**: Every run records which consent authorized it, what was transmitted and when, to which provider and model, what was asked, what was answered, and whether the answer was the person's, a default, or seeded from a prior run. FEAT-110's history detail and FEAT-111's re-run rules read these rows rather than reconstructing them.
- **Security posture (D03)**: This milestone is explicitly unisolated. Nothing in this feature's code, UI, or documentation may describe the disclosure gate as a limit on what generated code can reach. The guarantees here are narrow and specific: what is transmitted is bounded, approved, recorded, and reproducible. What generated code can read on the host is FEAT-108's open problem and is not addressed here.
- **Deferred scope guard**: No code generation, prompt engineering for Python, or repair loop (FEAT-106) — this row supplies `recordDiagnosticTransmission` and stops. No verification or execution gates (FEAT-107), no Python runtime (FEAT-108), no artifact rendering (FEAT-109), no history views (FEAT-110), no templates or re-run mapping (FEAT-111) beyond the `finding_key` seeding this row needs for its own retries. No URL ingestion, scheduling, gamification, or tool registry (D08). No consent revocation UI, no retention or purge policy (D12 open).
- **Memory alignment**: No deviation from memory. The repository pattern, TypeBox validation on every input, Pino with its redaction rules, the typed error hierarchy, exact pinning (nothing new to pin), `ds.*` tokens, and the "never log cell contents" rule from FEAT-104 are all followed as written. Memory's Architecture section already anticipated this row twice — it names `request_clarification` as a custom tool and the `waiting` state as "entered when the agent escalates a clarification to the user"; this feature implements both as described. One **contract gap**, not a deviation, is recorded in §1 and closed by TASK-008: `AgentSessionOptions.customTools` is used by FEAT-102's TASK-007 and FEAT-103's `RunStrategy` but declared by neither.
